content.html:
On average, low-profile microwaves cost around $500+, which is more expensive than the traditional countertop models. So what's the reason behind it?

Low-profile microwaves appear more costly because they offer equivalent functionality to the standard models but consume less space. When manufacturers incorporate modern technologies into a smaller form factor, it increases production price which increases the consumer's retail price.

Let's dive deeper to explore the factors contributing to low-profile microwaves' high price tag and some alternatives to consider if low-profile microwaves currently don't fit your budget.

The Cost of Low Profile Microwaves Explained

#1. Technology

Low-profile microwaves have started becoming popular in recent years. So they are built with modern technology. And some of their functions are not even available in the standard models of microwaves.

Low-profile microwaves are good at ventilation. They sit higher over the cooktop than full-sized over-the-range microwaves for effective ventilation. To achieve adequate air extraction low profile over the range microwaves must house a better motor for improved CFM. Once again all this tech must be squeed into a smaller form factor.

This is vital because the ventilation of the low-profile microwaves will remove any bad odor, oil vapor, and unwanted steam from the air – giving you a more pleasant cooking experience, and better air quality in your home.

These compact microwaves not only provide ventilation for the space above the range, but they also have low heating emitting LED lights that illuminate the range top – so that you can have a better view of your cooking area.

#2. It Offers Standard Features But Consumes Less Space

You can place a low-profile microwave on top of your counter region without taking up too much room. A low-profile microwave is as long as your range but smaller than the standard microwave. 

Low-profile microwaves often measure slightly over 10 inches in height, needing a narrower aperture in the cabinets above your stove. If you're short on counter space but want a microwave, this is a great way to get one without sacrificing storage space.

They have additional room from front to back and protrude a little from the cabinet. These low-profile microwaves are ideal for homes with limited counter space above the range, yet they perform the same functions as a standard microwave.

So, in short, these additional features enhance the USP of the low-profile microwave. And as their perceived value increases, prices naturally increase.

#3. Reasonable Demand But Less Competition

If we talk about low-profile microwaves, there are not many players on the market competing with each other. Mainly, only three major brands are making the low-profile microwave as follows:

  1. Whirlpool
  2. Kitchenaid
  3. Samsung

So competition is less, but the demand is relatively good in the market. Low-profile microwaves are solving the problems of the user. They take up less space and are beneficial in many ways. Check out this guide on whether you should get a low-profile microwave to learn about its benefits and more.

So as a result, most new homes nowadays come with a low-profile microwave.

Think about that for a second:

Demand is reasonable, but competition is less. So why won’t any company take advantage of the situation and make profits?

Although the companies like Whirlpool and Samsung are all reputed brands. But they are doing business at the end of the day and need resources to operate it. Hence, this could also be one of the reasons why low-profile microwaves are expensive these days.

How Much Do Microwaves Typically Cost?

The cost of microwaves varies based on factors like the type of microwave and its features.

If we go to the low end of the spectrum, microwaves are available as low as $100 to $180. The mid-range options are usually priced at $350 and above. However, if you are looking for high-end microwave models, expect to pay anywhere from $600 to $3000 and more.

The cost of low-profile microwaves starts from roughly $400 and can be more depending on the brand or the extra features they offer.

*Prices may fluctuate with time and are given for a general idea.

What Are The Best Alternatives To Low-Profile Microwaves?

If you need a great microwave but have a limited budget, you may utilize the low-cost choices as an alternative to fulfill your requirements.

The usual rate for less expensive microwave versions is roughly $100, and typically, countertop models are more prevalent in this price range. 

Over-the-range microwaves can be found for approximately $150. On the other hand, you can find the built-in variants for roughly $180. 

These alternative microwaves are suitable for those on a tight budget but need a microwave only for occasional or simple reheating. Also, it is common in college residence halls. 

It is also essential to note that you receive a model with basic functionality at this pricing range. For example, rotating the food as it cooks is a standard feature.

There may be dedicated buttons for popcorn, roasted potatoes, and defrosting, but otherwise, there are no frills. Similarly, ventilation systems are uncommon in these models.

Not pleased with the low-budget models? Then go for mid-range models:

You can get a considerably good quality mid-range microwave for roughly $350. There is a nice balance between price and functionality in mid-range microwaves, making them ideal for most kitchens.

They have similar functions as the cheaper models but usually, have larger storage space. In addition, more types of food, such as vegetables, drinks, and meat, are included in the shortcut keys. 

At this price range, you can also get over-the-counter models that include an exhaust fan to help keep the air in the kitchen flowing freely. 

The ventilation is often only two settings and is rather basic in this price category. But still a better upgrade than going with low-end models that don't come with any ventilation.

You may find extras like racks for more cooking area, and kid locks to keep young fingers off the keypad on some mid-range versions. You can also get bigger versions with more power in this price range.
